response:
The Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) measures the proportion of total variance in an outcome that is attributable to between-group (level-2) differences, as opposed to within-group (individual-level) variation. In multilevel modeling, it tells you how similar observations within the same cluster are compared to observations across clusters.

The formula is:

ICC = σ²_u / (σ²_u + σ²_e)

where σ²_u is the between-cluster (random intercept) variance and σ²_e is the within-cluster (residual) variance.

An ICC of 0 means cluster membership explains none of the variance — observations within a cluster are no more similar to each other than to observations in other clusters. An ICC of 1 means all variance is between clusters — everyone within a cluster has identical outcomes. In practice, ICCs in social science data often fall in the 0.05–0.25 range, and even small values (e.g., 0.05) can meaningfully affect standard errors, motivating the use of multilevel models.
